1. Heard Sri Vivek Srivastava, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Krishna Kumar Shukla, learned counsel for the informant as well as Sri Arun Kumar Mishra, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
2. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.51 of 2024, under Sections 376, 506, 313 I.P.C., Police Station- Tharwai, District- Prayagraj, during the pendency of trial.
PROSECUTION
STORY:
3. The applicant is stated to have committed rape with the victim when she had gone out to purchase vegetables by taking her in an orchard.

The applicant is stated to have threatened her to take her life,

RIVAL CONTENTIONS:
(Arguments on behalf of applicant)
4. The applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
5. The FIR is delayed by about three months and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
The victim is 20 years of age.
The allegations are per se false.
The prosecution story does not stand corroborated by any medical evidence as it is also stated that three months old pregnancy of the victim is terminated due to the said act of the applicant.
6. The victim is used to complaining against several persons of similar nature, as such the applicant is entitled for bail.
The instant FIR has just been instituted on the eve of his marriage which was scheduled to be solemnized on 17.4.2024.
7. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
8. There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 8.3.2024 and is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.

(Arguments on behalf of opposite party/State)
9.

The bail application has been opposed on the ground that the FIR is not delayed as the application before the police station was moved on 21.12.2023 itself, i.e. on the next date of the offence, but under the influence of the applicant the said FIR has not been instituted on time.
10. The statement of the doctor who had treated the victim indicates that there was possibility of internal injuries in the womb of the victim.

The affidavit of the father-in-law of the victim has deliberately been filed to show that victim had filed various complaints against other persons, but there is no evidence of any FIR being instituted by the victim.

CONCLUSION:
11. The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.

A person's right to life and liberty,
guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because he or she is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.

sentences.text: Learned AGA has not shown any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
12. It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned AGA for the State.

13. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record and taking into consideration that there is no injury to corroborate the prosecution story coupled with the fact that the FIR is delayed, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

14. Let the applicant- Ankush Bhartiya involved in aforementioned case crime number be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
(ii). The applicant will not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.
(iii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
(iv) The applicant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected of the commission of which he is suspected.

(v) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
15. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.
16.

It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
